To prevent mealybug spread in cassava, collect planting cuttings from a known mealybug-free area (not during the dry season), cut off the top and bottom 10-20cm of each stem, then soak the remaining cuttings in hot (not boiling) water for 5 minutes before cooling and planting.

To prevent Fall Armyworm infestation, use high-quality, disease-free seed, avoid late or staggered planting, and increase plant diversity in your plots (for example intercropping) to make maize less attractive to armyworm moths.

To manage potato bacterial wilt, uproot and remove infected plants from the field, buy certified disease-free seed potatoes, rotate potatoes/tomatoes/peppers/eggplants with maize, bananas, beans, cassava, or millet, remove all volunteer potato tubers after harvest, and keep field tools clean.

To reduce Brown Leaf Spot in cassava, use good, healthy planting stock, destroy infected crop husks after harvest, and plant early so the crop grows vigorously; if healthy planting material isn't available, dip cassava stems in a diluted fungicide before planting.

To free cassava cuttings of mealybugs before planting, heat water until it is too hot to hold a finger in for more than five seconds (about 60C), then dip the cuttings in this hot water for one minute only - do not soak longer, as this can kill the cuttings too.

To manage mango bacterial black spot, plant tolerant varieties such as Heidi or Sensation, plant windbreaks to reduce rain splash, burn infected fruits and dead branches, prune to improve airflow and light in the canopy, and apply copper sprays or fungicides regularly.
